title: 2026-10-22_Octopus-Rex_Botnet_Investigation_4e4
description: Investigate and respond to the Octopus-Rex botnet activity, focusing on identifying suspicious services, understanding their behavior, and determining their persistence mechanisms.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents. Your task is to investigate and respond to these issues.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:

- Host: victim

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication?
levels.solution: Check running services and look for unusual network connections. The suspicious service is likely the bot-beacon service. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and look for unusual network connections.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Traffic Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service generating abnormal volumes of network traffic?
levels.solution: Examine network connections and look for services making multiple connections to the same destination. The service generating abnormal traffic is likely the bot-flood service. Use the command `ss -tulnp` to examine network connections.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine network connections and look for services making multiple connections to the same destination.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the service or mechanism used for persistence?
levels.solution: Check systemd timers and services for any suspicious entries. The persistence mechanism is likely the system-update-checker.timer service. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to check systemd timers.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check systemd timers and services for any suspicious entries.
